newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CME hogs, pork bellies end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CME hogs, pork bellies end sharply higher.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures closed sharply higher in nearby contracts and mixed in deferreds on support linked to light hog marketings and higher cash prices, traders said.

Hog futures closed 1.050 cent per lb higher to 0.450 lower with July up 1.050 at 81.925 cents. Pork bellies finished up 2.325 to off 0.450 with July up most at 81.325 cents. Only some next year contracts posted losses in pork complex pits.

Much of the strength in both pits reflected the return to light hog markets and a firmer tone to cash pork prices, especially with the slaughter rates slipping back to below-year ago levels, traders said.

Hog futures found commercial support on projections for higher cash hog prices again Wednesday on reduced runs. Wholesale pork prices also rose after losses last week and speculation increased that Japan business may now be developing. The sentiment circulated after USDA estimated last week that sales to Japan were less than earlier expected.

"That 'safe guard' goes off June 30 (in Japan), and even though everyone was bad mouthing (exports), I'm wondering if people are thinking there might be something coming once the 'safe guard' goes off," said Karen Curry, of Rosenthal Collins.
Curry also noted that although Japan is working through its frozen supply, the fresh chilled supply is tight. The chilled market is where the U.S. can become a key supplier, she said.
Floor sources also cited technical support after the market gapped higher at the start.

Rand Financials bought July late and E.D.&F. Man bought July. Lind-Waldock, R.J. O'Brien, and Cargill Investor Services were early buyers. In hog options, commission houses were on both sides of July 78 to 82 puts and sold July 84 calls. Lind-Waldock sold October 62 puts, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures again advanced into the close before local profit taking developed at the closing bell. Much of the mixed support reflected the light hog runs and resulting lighter slaughter this week as well as a firmer tone to cash pork bellies, traders said.

Expectations for a bullish USDA Cold Storage report Friday also lent support and offset concern that futures continued to offer a hedge and expectations of net storings last week in approved warehouses, they said.

Trade estimates on USDA's data for frozen pork bellies in U.S. warehouses May 31 ranged from 53.7 to 57.7 million lbs. The estimates compare with 63.5 million lbs on hand last year and the record low for that period of 54.98 million lbs set in 1973.

After the close, the CME reported a net in-movement last week at CME-approved warehouses outside chicago of 1.117 million lbs. This compared with analyst estimated of unchanged to in 500,000 lbs and pit trader estimates of around 1.0 million lbs.
Refco bought late in some light buy stops. Demand much of the day came from locals and commission houses, pit sources said.
